Week 12: Multi-Chamber Hardware Build

Fully implemented and tested the 7-channel MOSFET LED driver circuit on breadboard, completed soldering, and validated the 40-day automated lighting schedule for the 3-chamber mushroom growth experiment.

Completed
July 2026 Week 12 of 14 7-Channel Driver EEE · University of Peradeniya
🔧
✅ Soldering Complete — Circuit Fully Built

7-MOSFET low-side driver circuit bench-tested and soldered. Signal isolation verified across all 3 experimental channels + 1 control. System ready for 40-day growth cycle deployment.

What We Did This Week

  • Built the full 7-channel MOSFET low-side switching network on breadboard using IRLZ44N N-Channel MOSFETs — controlling 3 experimental chambers (Blue + Green each) and 1 control chamber (White).
  • Updated physical setup to an open-shelf racking framework to prevent CO₂ buildup and maintain cross-ventilation across all chambers.
  • Introduced black polythene sheets to isolate the 3 experimental replication zones and 1 control group without blocking airflow.
  • Implemented common ground bus connecting 12V supply negative, ESP32 GND, and all 7 MOSFET sources — resolving previous LED flickering during OFF states.
  • Verified logic-level gate driving — IRLZ44N fully saturates from ESP32's 3.3V GPIO output without needing additional gate driver ICs.
  • Configured 5 kHz PWM at 8-bit resolution — allowing smooth transitions between 25% brightness (duty 64/255) for pinning and 100% (255/255) for fruiting.
  • Completed soldering of the full circuit and bench-tested both the test sequence code and the 40-day NTP-synced schedule code.

Hardware Test — Circuit Demo Video

Circuit test sequence — White + Green LEDs activate at t=0, Blue LEDs start at t=2.5 min. Each group: 1 min ON → 30s OFF → 30s ON → OFF. Validates all 7 MOSFET channels independently.

Code Snippets

Test Sequence Code — validates all channels with timed ON/OFF pulses:

test_sequence.ino C++ / Arduino 
// ESP32 LED channel test sequence
// White+Green: start at t=0 | Blue: start at t=2.5 min
// Each group: ON 1min → OFF 30s → ON 30s → OFF (stays off)

const int PIN_WHITE    = 7;
const int PIN_GREEN[3] = {7, 4, 2};   // D7, D4, D2
const int PIN_BLUE[3]  = {8, 6, 3};   // D8, D6, D3

const unsigned long ON1_END  = 60000UL;   // 1 min
const unsigned long OFF1_END = 90000UL;   // +30 s
const unsigned long ON2_END  = 120000UL;  // +30 s
const unsigned long BLUE_DELAY = 150000UL;// 2.5 min

bool stateForElapsed(unsigned long elapsed) {
  if (elapsed < ON1_END)  return true;
  if (elapsed < OFF1_END) return false;
  if (elapsed < ON2_END)  return true;
  return false;
}

void loop() {
  unsigned long now = millis();
  bool wgOn = stateForElapsed(now);
  digitalWrite(PIN_WHITE, wgOn ? HIGH : LOW);
  for (int i=0; i<3; i++)
    digitalWrite(PIN_GREEN[i], wgOn ? HIGH : LOW);

  if (now >= BLUE_DELAY) {
    bool bOn = stateForElapsed(now - BLUE_DELAY);
    for (int i=0; i<3; i++)
      digitalWrite(PIN_BLUE[i], bOn ? HIGH : LOW);
  }
}

40-Day NTP Schedule Code — syncs to real time via WiFi, runs full growth cycle automatically:

schedule_40day.ino (key section) C++ / Arduino 
// White: ON 6am–6pm, day 1–40
// Green: ON 6am–6pm, day 1–10 only
// Blue:  ON 6am–6pm, day 11–40 only
// NTP synced to Sri Lanka (UTC+5:30). Start date saved to flash.

const char* NTP_SERVER   = "pool.ntp.org";
const long  GMT_OFFSET   = 5*3600 + 30*60; // UTC+5:30
const int   GREEN_LAST   = 10;  // green stops after day 10
const int   BLUE_FIRST   = 11;  // blue starts on day 11
const int   DAY_START    = 6;   // 6:00 am
const int   DAY_END      = 18;  // 6:00 pm

void loop() {
  time_t now; time(&now);
  struct tm t; localtime_r(&now, &t);

  int day = (int)((now - experimentStart) / 86400L) + 1;
  bool dt = (t.tm_hour >= DAY_START && t.tm_hour < DAY_END);

  digitalWrite(PIN_WHITE, dt && day<=40 ? HIGH:LOW);
  for(int i=0;i<3;i++) {
    digitalWrite(PIN_GREEN[i], dt&&day<=GREEN_LAST?HIGH:LOW);
    digitalWrite(PIN_BLUE[i],  dt&&day>=BLUE_FIRST ?HIGH:LOW);
  }
  delay(1000);
}

Hardware Verification Notes

⚡ Common Ground Bus

Strict shared GND between 12V supply, ESP32 GND, and all 7 MOSFET sources — resolved LED flickering during OFF states caused by floating voltage reference.

🔒 Pull-down Resistors (100kΩ)

Gate-to-GND pull-downs eliminate floating gate states during boot and standby — preventing random LED activation before firmware initialises.

📡 NTP Time Sync + Flash Storage

Start date is saved to ESP32 NVS flash — survives power loss and reboot without resetting the 40-day count. NTP resyncs every 6 hours to prevent clock drift.
